IPT.evidence_source: [/page/3/Text/15] The child is encouraged to develop further his or her ability to pay attention and observe his or her own thoughts and feelings. The aims and content are similar to those of the first session, although the child is now encouraged to make some judgements about potential causal links between mood, events and thoughts. [/page/3/Text/24] The child is encouraged to engage further in social activities and thus enhance self-esteem. More detailed discussion, including role play, focuses on specific social and interpersonal difficulties. Self-reinforcement may be used to encourage desirable activities. [/page/3/Text/26] The child is facilitated to distinguish between internal and external effects on mood and is asked to give examples of cognitions and events that usually precipitate depressed mood. Negative thoughts are then challenged by asking the child to provide 'evidence' that these are justified.
